Reproducing Tang, Shin & Jadhav (2023) from dandiset 000447¶

Paper. Tang W, Shin JD, Jadhav SP (2023). Geometric transformation of cognitive maps for generalization across hippocampal-prefrontal circuits. Cell Reports 42, 112246. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2023.112246. The claims file (claims/000447/10.1016-j.celrep.2023.112246.yaml) was written from the NIH author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC10124109) with its STAR Methods and supplement; the version of record was not read. Method details the claims file lacks were taken from the same text and from the paper's code, github.com/JadhavLab/GeometricTransformation at commit 5e55e69 (cited where used, in the cells and in nfn.py).

Dataset. DANDI:000447, version 0.250724.2224. The paper cites no version (its data statement says the data are on Brandeis servers, on request), so the most recent published version is pinned. The other published version, 0.230316.2133, holds the same five files; their spike times, unit electrodes, trial tables, epochs and positions are identical byte for byte (checked while preparing, not re-run here), and the file sizes differ by about 169 kB of metadata.

What the dandiset holds. One file per rat (AM2, JS17, JS21, ZT2, JS34) for the N-F-N' day: three W-track epochs, a trials table (start and end well, inbound or outbound, correct), 2D position with speed at 30 frames per second, sorted units (spike times and a tetrode number) and the 1.5 kHz LFP. It does not hold the de novo learning sessions, the three F-N-F'-N' rats, linearized positions, ripple or theta times, waveforms, or cell labels.

Outside inputs. None. The paper's code is read for method details only.

The blocked behaviour claims need the de novo learning sessions, which the dandiset does not hold and which the paper says are on Brandeis servers, available on request.

The smoothing width. The width of the 1D Gaussian that smooths the linearized rate maps is garbled in the paper's text (Methods, Spatial fields and linearization, "s = σ cm"), and the Methods give no smoothing for the single-trial maps of the manifolds. Every analysis on these maps is run at 8 cm (the 2D width given in the sentence before, the claims file's reading a) and at 4 and 2 cm. The claims file's rule for fig2d-pv-similarity (the outcome is that of 8 cm when the widths agree, and methods underspecified otherwise) is applied to every claim that uses the maps: where the widths give different outcomes, the claim is blocked as methods underspecified, with the result at every width. A claim that depends on a claim blocked this way is blocked for the same reason, with its results shown.

import os
import time
import warnings

# UMAP's numba code is compiled for the host CPU, and its optimization amplifies the rounding
# differences, so the embeddings differed between machines. Compile for a generic x86-64 target
# and fix the BLAS kernel and numpy's dispatch, before numpy and numba are imported.
os.environ["NUMBA_CPU_NAME"] = "generic"
os.environ["OPENBLAS_CORETYPE"] = "Haswell"
os.environ["NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES"] = "AVX512F AVX512CD AVX512_SKX AVX512_CLX AVX512_CNL AVX512_ICL AVX512_SPR"

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import nfn

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
started = time.time()
A = nfn.load_all()
for d in A:
    nfn.linearize(d)
BY = {d["animal"]: d for d in A}
SMOOTHS = (8.0, 4.0, 2.0)
MAPS = {(d["animal"], s, ep): nfn.rate_maps(d, ep, np.arange(d["n_units"]), smooth_cm=s)
        for d in A for s in SMOOTHS for ep in range(3)}
print(f"loaded {len(A)} files from dandiset {nfn.DANDISET_ID} version {nfn.DANDISET_VERSION}, "
      f"linearized and mapped in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

The units table has only spike times and an electrodes column. By the NWB format that column holds row indices of the electrodes table, but its values run up to 64 in ZT2, whose table has 128 rows (two per tetrode), and up to 32 in the others (62 to 64 rows): the values are tetrode numbers. Read as tetrode numbers through the label column, the regions give CA1 and PFC counts close to the paper's (next cells, and claims cells-per-session and manifold-cell-counts); read as row indices, the counts differ by up to 32 units per animal (ZT2). The tetrode reading is used throughout; the format error is recorded as a finding. There are no waveforms, cell numbers within a tetrode, or putative interneuron labels.

Each file has three epochs, read as N, F and N' in that order, as the dandiset's description says. All spikes lie inside the three epochs. Positions are in cm (the W-maze is about 80 by 80 cm in the Methods); the third position column is the speed in cm/s, as the comment says. Some units are listed after the tetrode-ordered block and have no spike in N; they were clustered only in later epochs.

# The paper's code excludes putative interneurons by hard-coded (tetrode, cell) lists. The files
# carry no cell numbers; numbering the units of a tetrode in their order in the file shows what the
# lists would pick.
EXCLUDE = {"AM2": [(6, 9)], "JS21": [(6, 3), (6, 6), (6, 7), (6, 8), (7, 1), (21, 1), (22, 1), (25, 1)],
           "JS17": [(6, 1), (7, 1)], "ZT2": [(31, 1), (31, 5), (32, 2), (27, 1), (14, 10)], "JS34": []}
for d in A:
    n, rate = nfn.epoch_counts(d)
    ue = d["unit_electrode_value"]
    order = np.array([(ue[:i] == v).sum() + 1 for i, v in enumerate(ue)])
    for tet, cell in EXCLUDE[d["animal"]]:
        hit = np.where((ue == tet) & (order == cell))[0]
        desc = ", ".join(f"{d['unit_region'][i]} unit, rate N/F/N' {np.round(rate[i], 1).tolist()} Hz" for i in hit) or "no such unit"
        print(f"{d['animal']} listed ({tet},{cell}): {desc}")
    hi = np.where((rate >= nfn.CA1_MAX_RATE).any(1) & (d["unit_region"] == "CA1"))[0]
    print(f"   {d['animal']} CA1 units at 7 Hz or more in some epoch: "
          + "; ".join(f"tetrode {ue[i]} #{order[i]} {np.round(rate[i], 1).tolist()}" for i in hi))

Where the code's lists name a unit that exists, it is mostly a CA1 unit firing at 14 to 45 Hz (JS17 (6,1); JS21 (6,3), (6,6), (7,1), (25,1); ZT2 (32,2) and (27,1), the latter 14.7 Hz in F only), which supports the tetrode reading. Other entries name tetrodes without units (JS21 21 and 22, ZT2 31) or low-rate units, so the numbering by order is not exact. The code's own rule, CA1 mean rate below 7 Hz in the epoch, removes every listed CA1 unit in the epochs where it fires at 7 Hz or more; ZT2 (27,1) stays in N and N', where it fires at 0 and 1.4 Hz. The lists are not applied. PFC units are kept whatever their rate, as the code keeps every unit tagged PFC.

# The acquisition ElectricalSeries and the processed LFP: are they the same recording?
for d in A:
    import h5py, remfile
    f = h5py.File(remfile.File(urls[d["animal"]][1]), "r")
    a = f["acquisition/ElectricalSeries/data"]
    b = f["processing/ecephys/LFP/ElectricalSeries/data"]
    ta = f["acquisition/ElectricalSeries/timestamps"]
    same = all(np.array_equal(a[i:i + 200, :], b[i:i + 200, :]) for i in (0, a.shape[0] // 2, a.shape[0] - 200))
    rate = 1 / np.median(np.diff(ta[:20000]))
    print(f"{d['animal']}: shapes {a.shape} and {b.shape}, sampling {rate:.0f} Hz, identical in 3 slices: {same}, "
          f"stored at different offsets: {a.id.get_offset() != b.id.get_offset()}")

The acquisition/ElectricalSeries is a second, byte-identical copy of the 1.5 kHz LFP (in every file, at all three slices tested), not the 30 kHz spike-band recording. The LFP is not used here: the analysis needs spikes and position only, apart from the exclusion of sharp-wave ripples, which is not done (see the summary).

# Linearization: idealized W paths from the well positions (nfn.build_skeleton, an assumption,
# as the paths are not in the dandiset). Paper: "2-m-long linearized trajectories" (Figure 2B).
rows = []
for d in A:
    for ep in range(3):
        m = (d["epoch_of_sample"] == ep) & (d["speed"] > nfn.MIN_SPEED) & np.isfinite(d["lin_offset"])
        rows.append({"animal": d["animal"], "epoch": nfn.EPOCHS[ep],
                     "OUT_L/IN_L length (cm)": round(d["track_length"][(ep, 1)]),
                     "OUT_R/IN_R length (cm)": round(d["track_length"][(ep, 3)]),
                     "run samples on a trajectory": int(m.sum()),
                     "distance to path, median (cm)": round(np.median(d["lin_offset"][m]), 1),
                     "90th pct": round(np.percentile(d["lin_offset"][m], 90), 1),
                     "99th pct": round(np.percentile(d["lin_offset"][m], 99), 1)})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 5, figsize=(16, 9))
for i, d in enumerate(A):
    for ep in range(3):
        ax = axes[ep, i]
        m = (d["epoch_of_sample"] == ep) & (d["speed"] > nfn.MIN_SPEED)
        ax.plot(d["x"][m], d["y"][m], ",", alpha=0.3)
        for t in (1, 3):
            p = d["templates"][(ep, t)]
            ax.plot(p[:, 0], p[:, 1], "r-")
        ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_title(f"{d['animal']} {nfn.EPOCHS[ep]}", fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("All run positions are plotted (none outside the axes).")

The idealized paths follow the arms the rats ran (figure). Every trajectory is 180 to 220 cm long, consistent with the paper's 2-m trajectories, and the median distance from a run position to its path is about 5 cm (the tracks are about 7 cm wide in the Methods).

# Clock check: decode N' positions from N' spikes with N' templates (in-sample) after shifting all
# spike times. If spikes and position share a clock the error is smallest at no shift.
rows = []
for d in A:
    for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
        cells = nfn.included(d, reg, 2)
        m = MAPS[(d["animal"], 8.0, 2)]
        cells = cells[nfn.peak_rate({t: (m[t][0], m[t][1][cells]) for t in m}) >= nfn.PEAK_HZ]
        tm = {t: (m[t][0], m[t][1][cells]) for t in m}
        row = {"animal": d["animal"], "region": reg, "cells": len(cells)}
        for sh in (-2.0, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 2.0):
            d2 = dict(d); d2["spikes"] = [s + sh for s in d["spikes"]]
            df, _ = nfn.decode_session(d2, 2, cells, tm, n_shuffles=1, restrict_track=True)
            row[f"shift {sh:+.1f} s"] = round(df.error.median(), 1)
        rows.append(row)
clock = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Median in-sample decoding error (cm, decode restricted to the current trajectory):")
print(clock.to_string(index=False))
print("Rows whose smallest error is at zero shift:",
      int((clock.filter(like="shift").idxmin(axis=1) == "shift +0.0 s").sum()), "of", len(clock))

In every animal and region the in-sample decoding error is smallest with no shift and grows when the spikes are shifted by 0.5 or 2 s, so spikes and position share the clock in N'. Spikes and the trial table are checked the same way by the trial-by-trial decoding of Figure 2F below, which uses the trial boundaries.

Behaviour¶

fig1c-familiar-above-novel¶

In both groups of rats, performance in the familiar environment is higher than in the novel one whatever the order of exposure (N-F-N' group in Figure 1C, F-N-F'-N' group in Figure S1C).

The de novo sessions and the F-N-F'-N' rats are not in the dandiset. The test is run on N, F and N' alone: a repeated-measures ANOVA over three sessions in place of the five of Figure 1C, with Tukey's test on its error term. The novel curve is estimated on N and N' run together and the familiar curve on F alone (cal_behavperform.m runs the novel sessions together; its familiar run would include the de novo days, which are missing). The state-space model's background probability is 1/3 (cal_behavperform.m).

Result: not reproduced (N-F-N' rats only). On N, F and N' the repeated-measures ANOVA gives F(2,8) = 1.08, p = 0.383, and Tukey's test does not put F above N (difference 0.060, p = 0.70). F is above N in four rats (0.078 to 0.222) and below it in ZT2 (-0.282), whose F session has 24 trials at 0.50 correct. Estimating each session alone gives the same (p = 0.46). ZT2's trials table is complete: counted from position, ZT2 made 22 well-to-well transits in F against 24 rows, the trials tile the whole 1554-s epoch, and ZT2 spent the smallest fraction of any session above 5 cm/s there (0.33), so the low count is the rat's behaviour, not a gap in the table. The F-N-F'-N' rats of Figure S1C are not in the dandiset, and the de novo sessions of the paper's five-group ANOVA are missing.

cells-per-session¶

Cells are units with more than 100 spikes in the session, CA1 units with a mean rate below 7 Hz in it (claims file; the Methods say "at least 100", which is shown as a variant).

Remapping (Figure 2, S3, S4)¶

fig2d-pv-similarity¶

PFC population-vector similarity across environments (F-N') is as high as across repeated exposures to the novel environment (N-N'), while CA1 PV similarity is lower across environments than within the novel environment, where the CA1 map is reinstated.

As cal_PVsimilarity.m: cells passing the inclusion rules in either session of the pair and spatially tuned (peak of the linearized map at least 3 Hz in either session); each track's map on 101 bins of normalized length, interior NaN runs filled, the four tracks concatenated, NaN set to 0; Pearson r per bin over cells; per animal the mean over bins. Smoothing 8 cm (reading a), 4 and 2 cm (variants).

In [10]:
def pv_cells(d, reg, e1, e2, s=8.0, rule=">="):
    cells = np.union1d(nfn.included(d, reg, e1), nfn.included(d, reg, e2))
    m1, m2 = MAPS[(d["animal"], s, e1)], MAPS[(d["animal"], s, e2)]
    R1 = nfn.normalized({t: (m1[t][0], m1[t][1][cells]) for t in m1})
    R2 = nfn.normalized({t: (m2[t][0], m2[t][1][cells]) for t in m2})
    if rule == ">= native":   # variant: peak on the native 2-cm maps, not on the 101 resampled bins
        p1 = nfn.peak_rate({t: (m1[t][0], m1[t][1][cells]) for t in m1}); p2 = nfn.peak_rate({t: (m2[t][0], m2[t][1][cells]) for t in m2})
    else:
        p1, p2 = np.nanmax(R1, 1), np.nanmax(R2, 1)
    tuned = ((p1 >= 3) | (p2 >= 3)) if rule.startswith(">=") else ((p1 > 3) | (p2 > 3))
    return cells[tuned], R1[tuned], R2[tuned]

def pv_bins(d, reg, e1, e2, s=8.0, rule=">=", cells_mask=None):
    cells, R1, R2 = pv_cells(d, reg, e1, e2, s, rule)
    R1, R2 = np.nan_to_num(R1), np.nan_to_num(R2)
    return np.array([np.corrcoef(R1[:, i], R2[:, i])[0, 1] if R1[:, i].std() > 0 and R2[:, i].std() > 0 else np.nan
                     for i in range(R1.shape[1])])

GROUPS = ["CA1 N-N'", "CA1 F-N'", "PFC N-N'", "PFC F-N'"]
PAIRS = {"N-N'": (0, 2), "F-N'": (1, 2), "F-N": (1, 0)}
for s, rule in [(8.0, ">="), (4.0, ">="), (2.0, ">="), (8.0, ">"), (8.0, ">= native")]:
    M = pd.DataFrame([[np.nanmean(pv_bins(d, g.split()[0], *PAIRS[g.split()[1]], s=s, rule=rule)) for g in GROUPS] for d in A],
                     index=nfn.ANIMALS, columns=GROUPS)
    ncell = pd.DataFrame([[len(pv_cells(d, g.split()[0], *PAIRS[g.split()[1]], s, rule)[0]) for g in GROUPS] for d in A],
                         index=nfn.ANIMALS, columns=GROUPS)
    a, t = nfn.rm_anova_tukey(M.values, GROUPS)
    print(f"--- smoothing {s:g} cm, peak rule {rule} 3 Hz ---")
    print("mean PV similarity per animal:"); print(M.round(3))
    print("tuned cells per animal and pair:", ncell.to_dict("list"))
    print(f"repeated-measures ANOVA F({a['df'][0]},{a['df'][1]}) = {a['F']:.2f}, p = {a['p']:.2g}")
    print(t[((t.A == "CA1 N-N'") & (t.B == "CA1 F-N'")) | ((t.A == "PFC N-N'") & (t.B == "PFC F-N'"))].round(4).to_string(index=False))

Result: reproduced. With 8-cm smoothing, CA1 PV similarity is 0.419 to 0.652 within the novel room (N-N') and -0.138 to 0.239 across rooms (F-N') in the five rats; PFC is 0.727 to 0.952 (N-N') and 0.647 to 0.943 (F-N'). The repeated-measures ANOVA gives F(3,12) = 67.53, p = 8.8e-08; Tukey's test puts CA1 F-N' below N-N' (difference 0.473, p = 0.0001) and finds no PFC difference (p = 0.99). The 4-cm and 2-cm widths, the code's "> 3 Hz" rule and the peak taken on the native 2-cm maps give the same outcome (CA1 p <= 0.0001, PFC p >= 0.99).

figs3a-ca1-global-remapping and figs3a-pfc-similar-ca1-lower¶

CA1 spatial similarity between the two environments is no different from that of cell-ID shuffles, that is, CA1 remaps globally.

Single-cell rate overlap and spatial correlation of PFC cells across environments (F-N') are as large as across repeated exposures to the novel environment (N-N'), whereas in CA1 they are lower across environments.

Cells of the PV analysis (fig2d). Spatial similarity is the Pearson r of a cell's two concatenated normalized maps over bins valid in both. Rate overlap is the lower over the higher mean rate, with the mean rate read as (a) the mean of the linearized map or (b) spikes over run time (speed above 5 cm/s on a trajectory). The shuffle pairs each cell's F map with another cell's N' map of the same animal (a random derangement within the animal; the Methods say "a different cell"). One-way ANOVA with Tukey's test over N-N', F-N' and shuffle, per region and measure. The shuffle is one draw; the result over 100 draws is shown too.

In [11]:
def remap_measures(d, reg, e1, e2, rng=None, s=8.0):
    cells, R1, R2 = pv_cells(d, reg, e1, e2, s)
    dt = nfn._sample_dt(d)
    run = []
    for ep in (e1, e2):
        m = nfn._run_mask(d, ep); T = dt[m].sum(); tt = d["t"]
        run.append(np.array([m[np.clip(np.searchsorted(tt, d["spikes"][u]), 0, len(tt) - 1)].sum() / T for u in cells]))
    if rng is not None:
        k = len(cells); perm = np.arange(k)
        while k > 1 and np.any(perm == np.arange(k)):
            perm = rng.permutation(k)
        R2, run[1] = R2[perm], run[1][perm]
    ma, mb = np.nanmean(R1, 1), np.nanmean(R2, 1)
    sc = []
    for i in range(len(cells)):
        ok = np.isfinite(R1[i]) & np.isfinite(R2[i])
        sc.append(stats.pearsonr(R1[i][ok], R2[i][ok])[0] if ok.sum() > 2 and R1[i][ok].std() > 0 and R2[i][ok].std() > 0 else np.nan)
    return pd.DataFrame({"overlap_map": np.minimum(ma, mb) / np.maximum(ma, mb),
                         "overlap_run": np.minimum(*run) / np.maximum(*run), "spatial_r": sc})

Result: reproduced. For the CA1 spatial correlation, Tukey's test finds no difference between F-N' and the cell-ID shuffle (F-N' higher by 0.074, p = 0.075). The margin is thin: over 100 shuffle draws p falls below 0.05 in 13 of them (median p 0.29), and F-N' is always higher than the shuffle (by 0.014 to 0.105). The 4-cm and 2-cm widths give the same outcome (p = 0.21 and 0.40). One of five rats (JS17, median r 0.31) keeps some CA1 spatial correlation across rooms.

CA1 F-N' is below N-N' in spatial correlation (difference 0.524, p < 0.0001) but not in rate overlap (p = 0.32 and 0.45), so the claim holds for one measure. Result: reproduced. With bins pooled over rats (8 cm), PFC F-N' exceeds F-N (0.836 against 0.774, Tukey p < 0.0001), CA1 F-N and F-N' do not differ (0.062 and 0.045, p = 0.065), and CA1 F-N' is below N-N' (0.517, p < 0.0001). PFC F-N' is below N-N' (difference 0.019, p = 0.0001; the paper reports p = 0.0013). The 4-cm and 2-cm widths give the same outcome (CA1 F-N against F-N' p = 0.098 and 0.26).

figs3d-pfc-similarity-over-trials¶

Over trials in the novel environment, PFC similarity to the familiar map rises from the first to the last trial, while CA1 similarity does not change.

Single-trial maps (2-cm bins, smoothed at 8, 4 and 2 cm as the session maps) of each trajectory pass in the novel environment against the session-averaged F maps of the same trajectory, over the tuned cells (peak at least 3 Hz in F or in the novel sessions); per-bin PV similarity on 101 normalized bins. A trial is kept when at least 80% of these cells fire during its run samples (legend). The paper does not say how trials are numbered or which is "last". Here the kept trials of each animal are ranked in order; trial ranks 1 to K enter the test, K being the smallest number of kept trials over the animals that have any, and "last" is (i) rank K or (ii) each animal's own final kept trial (ranks 1 to K - 1 and the final trials as the groups). Readings for the novel trials: (a) N then N', (b) N, (c) N'. One-way ANOVA over ranks on per-bin values, Tukey's test of first against last. The session each kept trial comes from is shown for reading (a).

SORTED = {d["animal"]: [np.sort(x) for x in d["spikes"]] for d in A}
rows = []
for s in SMOOTHS:
    for d in A:
        tr = d["trials"]
        mF = MAPS[(d["animal"], s, 1)]
        for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
            for name, eps in (("N then N'", [0, 2]), ("N", [0]), ("N'", [2])):
                cells = np.union1d(nfn.included(d, reg, 1), np.concatenate([nfn.included(d, reg, e) for e in eps]))
                pkF = nfn.peak_rate({t: (mF[t][0], mF[t][1][cells]) for t in mF})
                pkN = np.max([nfn.peak_rate({t: (MAPS[(d["animal"], s, e)][t][0], MAPS[(d["animal"], s, e)][t][1][cells]) for t in mF}) for e in eps], 0)
                cells = cells[(pkF >= 3) | (pkN >= 3)]
                order = 0
                for e in eps:
                    for i in tr[(tr.epoch == e) & (tr.track > 0)].index:
                        order += 1
                        track = int(tr.loc[i, "track"])
                        run = nfn._run_mask(d, e, track, i)
                        tt = d["t"][run]
                        if len(tt) == 0:
                            continue
                        ss_ = SORTED[d["animal"]]
                        active = np.mean([np.searchsorted(ss_[u], tt[-1], "right") > np.searchsorted(ss_[u], tt[0], "left") for u in cells])
                        c, r = nfn.rate_maps(d, e, cells, smooth_cm=s, trial=i, track_only=track)[track]
                        pos = np.linspace(0, 1, 101)
                        X = np.nan_to_num(r[:, np.abs((c / c.max())[None, :] - pos[:, None]).argmin(1)])
                        cF, rF = mF[track]
                        Y = np.nan_to_num(rF[cells][:, np.abs((cF / cF.max())[None, :] - pos[:, None]).argmin(1)])
                        pv = np.array([np.corrcoef(X[:, b], Y[:, b])[0, 1] if X[:, b].std() > 0 and Y[:, b].std() > 0 else np.nan for b in range(101)])
                        rows.append({"smooth": s, "animal": d["animal"], "region": reg, "reading": name, "order": order, "epoch": nfn.EPOCHS[e],
                                     "active": active, "pv": pv})
TRI = pd.DataFrame(rows)
T8 = TRI[TRI.smooth == 8.0]
print("8 cm: passes and passes kept (at least 80% of tuned cells active):")
print(T8.groupby(["region", "reading", "animal"]).agg(passes=("order", "size"), kept=("active", lambda x: int((x >= 0.8).sum()))).unstack("animal"))
print("\n8 cm, N then N': kept passes per animal by session:")
print(T8[(T8.reading == "N then N'") & (T8.active >= 0.8)].groupby(["region", "animal", "epoch"]).size().unstack("epoch", fill_value=0))
S3D = []
for (s, reg, name), x in TRI[TRI.active >= 0.8].groupby(["smooth", "region", "reading"]):
    x = x.copy(); x["rank"] = x.groupby("animal").order.rank().astype(int)
    x["n_kept"] = x.groupby("animal")["rank"].transform("max")
    K = int(x.n_kept.min())
    # (i) ranks 1 to K, the last trial rank K (K the smallest number of kept passes over the animals)
    xi = x[x["rank"] <= K]
    groups = [np.concatenate(xi[xi["rank"] == k].pv.values) for k in range(1, K + 1)]
    a, t = nfn.anova_tukey(groups, [f"{k:02d}" for k in range(1, K + 1)])
    r = t[(t.group1 == "01") & (t.group2 == f"{K:02d}")]
    # (ii) ranks 1 to K - 1, and each animal's own final kept pass as the last trial
    groups2 = [np.concatenate(x[x["rank"] == k].pv.values) for k in range(1, K)] + [np.concatenate(x[x["rank"] == x.n_kept].pv.values)]
    names2 = [f"{k:02d}" for k in range(1, K)] + ["last"]
    if len(groups2) >= 2:
        a2, t2 = nfn.anova_tukey(groups2, names2)
        r2 = t2[((t2.group1 == "01") & (t2.group2 == "last")) | ((t2.group1 == "last") & (t2.group2 == "01"))]
        sign2 = 1 if r2.group1.iloc[0] == "01" else -1
        diff2, p2 = sign2 * r2.meandiff.iloc[0], r2["p-adj"].iloc[0]
    else:
        diff2, p2 = np.nan, np.nan
    S3D.append({"smooth": s, "region": reg, "reading": name, "animals": x.animal.nunique(), "K": K,
                "kept per animal": x.groupby("animal")["rank"].max().to_dict(),
                "trial 1 mean": np.nanmean(groups[0]), "trial K mean": np.nanmean(groups[-1]), "ANOVA p": a["p"],
                "(i) last - first": r.meandiff.iloc[0], "(i) Tukey p": r["p-adj"].iloc[0],
                "own last mean": np.nanmean(groups2[-1]), "(ii) last - first": diff2, "(ii) Tukey p": p2})
S3D = pd.DataFrame(S3D)
with pd.option_context("display.float_format", lambda v: f"{v:.3g}", "display.max_colwidth", 60):
    print(S3D.to_string(index=False))

Result: partially reproduced. The criterion asks for the result under each reading of which novel trials. PFC similarity rises from the first to the last trial under all three readings at 8 cm (N then N' 0.688 to 0.741, Tukey p = 0.0018; N 0.684 to 0.757, p < 0.0001; N' 0.738 to 0.782, p = 0.0074, with the last trial at rank K). CA1 does not change under N then N' (0.053 and 0.048, p = 1.0), but falls under N (0.136 to 0.033, p = 0.0014; three rats, as JS34 and ZT2 have no N pass with 80% of CA1 cells active) and under N' (0.114 to 0.002, p < 0.0001), so the CA1 part holds under one reading of three. Taking each animal's own final kept pass as the last trial gives the same for CA1 (N then N' p = 0.53, N p = 0.0001, N' p < 0.0001); for PFC it holds under N then N' and N (p = 0.0046 and 0.0015) but not N' (p = 1). Under N then N', CA1's kept passes of JS21, JS34 and ZT2 all come from N', so the first trials are N' passes for three of five rats. The 4-cm and 2-cm widths give the same outcome: CA1 falls under N and under N' with at least one of the two definitions of the last trial (p <= 0.0098), and PFC rises under N then N' and N (p < 0.0001), but not under N' at 2 cm (p = 0.44 and 1).

Result: blocked, methods underspecified (the smoothing width). At 8 cm Grubbs' test finds no outlier among the bins of either region, for F-N' and F-N, over all bins (p = 1 in every case) or per trajectory (smallest p 0.40), and the values at the well ends lie inside the range of the other bins (CA1 F-N' -0.100 to 0.224, PFC 0.723 to 0.901). The 4-cm width gives the same (smallest p 0.116). With 2 cm, Grubbs' test finds an outlier among the PFC F-N' bins (all bins p = 0.0070, per trajectory p = 0.0012), so the claim would not reproduce. The outcome changes with the width, which the paper's text does not fix, and the claims file's rule for that case (fig2d-pv-similarity) makes the claim methods underspecified.

Decoding (Figure 2E, 2F)¶

fig2e-ca1-error-familiar and fig2e-pfc-error-stable¶

Decoding with N' rate maps, CA1 position error is higher in F than in N, and in F no better than with cell-ID shuffled templates.

Decoding with N' rate maps, PFC position error is similar in N and F, and in both well above chance (below the cell-ID shuffles).

Decoder of the Methods (nfn.decode_session): templates are the N' maps (8 cm) of cells included in N' with a peak of at least 3 Hz; 200-ms windows every 150 ms (the Methods' "50 ms overlap"); bins on one trajectory, mean speed above 5 cm/s, more than 15 cm from a well, at least one cell firing; error along the four trajectories laid end to end. Shuffles permute the cell identities of the templates: (a) one shuffle, (b) the median over 100. Wilcoxon paired test of each bin against its shuffle; Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's test over (a) the four groups, (b) N and F per region. Variants: a 50-ms step (the code), 4 and 2 cm smoothing, and the decode restricted to the current trajectory. The theta restriction of the code cannot be run (no theta times in the dandiset).

In [17]:
def decode_all(s=8.0, seed=401, **kw):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed); out = []
    for d in A:
        for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
            cells = nfn.included(d, reg, 2); m = MAPS[(d["animal"], s, 2)]
            cells = cells[nfn.peak_rate({t: (m[t][0], m[t][1][cells]) for t in m}) >= nfn.PEAK_HZ]
            tm = {t: (m[t][0], m[t][1][cells]) for t in m}
            for ep in (0, 1):
                df, _ = nfn.decode_session(d, ep, cells, tm, rng=rng, **kw)
                df["animal"], df["region"], df["env"], df["cells"] = d["animal"], reg, nfn.EPOCHS[ep], len(cells)
                out.append(df)
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True)

def decode_stats(D):
    g = {(r, e): D[(D.region == r) & (D.env == e)] for r in ("CA1", "PFC") for e in ("N", "F")}
    a4, dn4 = nfn.kruskal_dunn([g[k].error for k in g], [f"{r} {e}" for r, e in g])
    out = {"KW4 p": a4["p"]}
    for r in ("CA1", "PFC"):
        out[f"{r} N median"] = g[(r, "N")].error.median(); out[f"{r} F median"] = g[(r, "F")].error.median()
        out[f"{r} Dunn4 N-F p"] = dn4.loc[f"{r} N", f"{r} F"]
        out[f"{r} KW2 N-F p"] = stats.kruskal(g[(r, "N")].error, g[(r, "F")].error).pvalue
        for e in ("N", "F"):
            x = g[(r, e)]
            out[f"{r} {e} shuffle median"] = x.error_shuffle_median.median()
            out[f"{r} {e} W(a) p"] = stats.wilcoxon(x.error, x.error_shuffle1).pvalue
            out[f"{r} {e} W(b) p"] = stats.wilcoxon(x.error, x.error_shuffle_median).pvalue
            out[f"{r} {e} mean error minus shuffle(b)"] = (x.error - x.error_shuffle_median).mean()
    return out

Decoder check¶

A check that the decoder works: N' is decoded with templates from the other half of the N' passes (alternate passes of each trajectory type), and for every decoded bin the decoded trajectory is compared with the current one, and with the current arm of the maze (OUT_L and IN_L run over the left arm, OUT_R and IN_R over the right arm).

In [19]:
# Decoder check: cross-validated decoding of N' (templates from half of the N' trials, decoding
# the other half), and the fraction of bins decoded onto the current trajectory and onto the
# current arm (OUT_L and IN_L share the left arm, OUT_R and IN_R the right arm).
ARM = {1: "L", 2: "L", 3: "R", 4: "R"}
def cv_decode(s=8.0, seed=404, **kw):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed); out = []
    for d in A:
        tbt = nfn.trials_of_track(d, 2)   # alternate passes of each trajectory type go to the two halves
        folds = tuple(np.concatenate([np.array(tbt[t][k::2], int) for t in nfn.TRACKS]) for k in (0, 1))
        for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
            cells = nfn.included(d, reg, 2); m = MAPS[(d["animal"], s, 2)]
            cells = cells[nfn.peak_rate({t: (m[t][0], m[t][1][cells]) for t in m}) >= nfn.PEAK_HZ]
            for k in (0, 1):
                mt = nfn.rate_maps(d, 2, cells, smooth_cm=s, trial=folds[1 - k])
                df, _ = nfn.decode_session(d, 2, cells, mt, rng=rng, n_shuffles=1, trials=folds[k], **kw)
                df["animal"], df["region"], df["env"] = d["animal"], reg, "N' (cross-validated)"
                out.append(df)
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True)
CV = cv_decode()
CVR = cv_decode(restrict_track=True)
allD = pd.concat([DEC, CV], ignore_index=True)
allD["on_track"] = allD.decoded_track == allD.track
allD["on_arm"] = allD.decoded_track.map(ARM) == allD.track.map(ARM)
summ = allD.groupby(["region", "env"]).agg(bins=("error", "size"), median_error=("error", "median"),
                                           on_trajectory=("on_track", "mean"), on_arm=("on_arm", "mean"))
onr = allD[allD.on_track].groupby(["region", "env"]).error.median().rename("median error when on the trajectory")
summ = summ.join(onr)
summ["N' cross-validated, restricted decoder median error"] = [CVR[CVR.region == r].error.median() if e.startswith("N'") else np.nan for r, e in summ.index]
print("Main decoder (Methods, 8 cm); chance on trajectory 0.25, on arm 0.5:")
print(summ.round(3).to_string())
print("\nPer animal, fraction on the current trajectory:")
print(allD.groupby(["region", "env", "animal"]).on_track.mean().unstack("animal").round(2).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. CA1 error is higher in F than in N (median 230 against 172 cm, Dunn p = 1.8e-140), in every variant. In F the CA1 error is not below the shuffle; it is above it (mean paired difference 8.8 cm), and the Wilcoxon test finds the difference under both shuffle readings (p = 2.4e-08 and 0.042), so the claim of no difference fails by the paper's test. The other widths give the same outcome: 4 cm differs under reading (a) (p = 3.4e-10; reading (b) p = 0.79), and 2 cm puts F slightly below the shuffle (-3.5 cm, p = 1.8e-08 and 0.0067). The decoder works: decoding N' with templates from the other half of its passes gives a median error of 12 cm (64% of bins on the current trajectory, against 0.25 by chance). In N, 43% of CA1 bins are decoded onto the current trajectory and 65% onto the current arm; the large median errors come from decodes onto the other trajectory of the same arm, which the criterion counts as far.

It is not similar in N and F: F is higher (Dunn p = 7.0e-06; N and F alone, p = 3.9e-06), in every variant (p 6.2e-05 to 1.4e-17). With the decode restricted to the current trajectory, F is lower than N (23.5 against 28.5 cm, p = 6.2e-05), so the sign of the difference depends on the decoder, but every variant finds one. Four of five rats have higher PFC median error in F (JS17 is lower). PFC bins are decoded onto the current trajectory in 42% of N bins and 38% of F bins (cross-validated N', 52%).

fig2f-switch-dynamics¶

After the switch from N to F, CA1 decoding error rises within the first trial, while PFC decoding error stays stable.

Bins of the decoder above, grouped by trial (a row of the trials table; bins pooled over rats). Readings of trial -1: (a) the last N trial, so that N trials -10 to -1 are the last ten; (b) the code's batch script as it runs, which takes the first ten N trials. Trials 1 to 10 are the first ten F trials. Kruskal-Wallis over the 20 trials with Dunn's test (Bonferroni over all pairs). Variant decoder of the code: 200-ms bins without overlap, no speed filter, at least 2 active cells, decode restricted to the current trajectory.

def by_trial(D):
    D = D.copy()
    D["k"] = -1
    for d in A:
        tr = d["trials"]
        for ep in (0, 1):
            ids = list(tr[tr.epoch == ep].index); pos = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(ids)}
            m = (D.animal == d["animal"]) & (D.env == nfn.EPOCHS[ep])
            D.loc[m, "k"] = [pos.get(t, -999) for t in D.loc[m, "trial"]]
            D.loc[m, "nk"] = len(ids)
    return D

def trial_labels(D, reading):
    """Trial label: F trials 1, 2, ... from the switch; N trials (a) -1 for the last N trial and
    back from it, (b) the code's first ten N trials labelled -10 to -1 (later N trials dropped)."""
    if reading == "a":
        n_lab = D.k - D.nk
    else:
        n_lab = np.where(D.k < 10, D.k - 10, -999)
    return np.where(D.env == "N", n_lab, D.k + 1)

def trial_tests(D, reading):
    D = D.copy()
    D["lab"] = trial_labels(D, reading)
    D = D[(D.lab >= -10) & (D.lab <= 10) & (D.lab != 0)]
    out = {}
    for r in ("CA1", "PFC"):
        x = D[D.region == r]; labs = sorted(x.lab.unique())
        a, dn = nfn.kruskal_dunn([x[x.lab == l].error for l in labs], labs)
        med = x.groupby("lab").error.median()
        out[r] = {"KW p": a["p"], "trial -1 median": med[-1], "trial 1 median": med[1], "n -1": int((x.lab == -1).sum()),
                  "n 1": int((x.lab == 1).sum()), "n trials -10 to -1": int((x.lab < 0).sum()), "Dunn -1 vs 1 p": dn.loc[-1, 1]}
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

Result: partially reproduced. The criterion asks for the result under each reading of trial -1. Under reading (a), trial -1 the last N trial, CA1 error rises from 182 to 223 cm between trial -1 and trial 1 (Dunn p = 0.0021), and PFC does not differ (149 and 200 cm, p = 0.12). Under reading (b), the code's first ten N trials labelled -10 to -1 (later N trials dropped), CA1 trial 1 is not above trial -1 (223 against 259 cm, p = 1), and PFC does not differ (p = 1). So the PFC part holds under both readings and the CA1 part under one. The other widths do not give more: at 4 cm CA1 rises under (a) (p = 0.0079) but PFC rises too (p = 0.0004), and at 2 cm CA1 does not rise under either reading (p = 0.30 and 1) while PFC is stable (p = 0.076 and 1). The code's decoder (variant) finds no CA1 rise under (a) (p = 1); under (b) both regions rise (p = 0.00027 and 0.0013). Calling the outcome partial at every width is a judgement: at 8 and 4 cm one part holds under each reading or one reading holds in full, but at 2 cm only the PFC claim of absence holds and CA1 rises under neither reading, which alone would be closer to not reproduced. Since the outcome is partial or worse at every width, and reproduced at none, the width rule does not block it.

Reward ramping (Figure S4)¶

figs4-ramping-fraction¶

Ramping cells make up 16.4% of CA1 cell samples (81 of 495) and 18.1% of PFC cell samples (115 of 636), a cell sample being one cell on one trajectory type.

A session map (8 cm) of a cell on a trajectory ramps when the regression of rate on the position traversed toward the reward, over the whole trajectory, has Pearson r > 0.5 and p < 0.05, its peak is at least 3 Hz and lies within 20 cm of the trajectory's end (Methods). Denominators: (a) cell samples of the three sessions pooled, (b) N' only, each over included cells with a valid map (at least 3 visited bins). Variants: 4 and 2 cm smoothing, and denominators restricted to tuned samples (peak at least 3 Hz).

def ramp_table(s):
    rows = []
    for d in A:
        for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
            for ep in range(3):
                m = MAPS[(d["animal"], s, ep)]
                for c in nfn.included(d, reg, ep):
                    for tr in nfn.TRACKS:
                        ok, rr, p, valid = nfn.ramping(m, c, tr)
                        pk = np.nanmax(m[tr][1][c]) if np.isfinite(m[tr][1][c]).any() else np.nan
                        rows.append({"animal": d["animal"], "region": reg, "ep": ep, "unit": c, "track": tr, "ramp": ok,
                                     "valid": valid, "r": rr, "tuned": pk >= 3})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

    for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
        for nm, eps in (("(a) all sessions", [0, 1, 2]), ("(b) N'", [2])):
            x = R[(R.region == reg) & R.ep.isin(eps) & R.valid]
            xt = x[x.tuned]
            print(f"smoothing {s:g} cm, {reg} {nm}: {x.ramp.sum()} of {len(x)} = {100 * x.ramp.mean():.1f}%; "
                  f"of tuned samples {xt.ramp.sum()} of {len(xt)} = {100 * xt.ramp.mean():.1f}%")

figs4-ramping-generalization¶

PFC ramping cells generalize their reward representation across environments, whereas CA1 ramping cells remap, and the generalization of ramping cells is similar to that of other cells in each region.

Ramping cell samples identified in N' (8 cm). Per animal and trajectory, the PV over its ramping samples and the PV over the other tuned cells of the PV analysis on that trajectory, per bin (101 normalized bins), for N-N' and F-N'; a PV needs at least 3 cells (an assumption: a correlation over 2 cells is always plus or minus 1). Bins pooled over rats and trajectories; Kruskal-Wallis over the 8 groups with Dunn's test. Variant: the ramping samples pooled over animals into one population per trajectory.

RN = RAMP[8.0]; RN = RN[(RN.ep == 2) & RN.ramp]
pos101 = np.linspace(0, 1, 101)
def track_norm(m, track, cells):
    c, r = m[track]; r = r[cells]
    out = nfn.normalized({t: (m[t][0], m[t][1][cells]) for t in m})
    k = list(nfn.TRACKS).index(track)
    return out[:, k * 101:(k + 1) * 101]
def bin_corr(X, Y):
    X, Y = np.nan_to_num(X), np.nan_to_num(Y)
    return np.array([np.corrcoef(X[:, b], Y[:, b])[0, 1] if X[:, b].std() > 0 and Y[:, b].std() > 0 else np.nan for b in range(X.shape[1])])
G8 = {}; counts = []
pooled = {}
for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
    for pair in ("N-N'", "F-N'"):
        e1, e2 = PAIRS[pair]
        for kind in ("ramping", "other"):
            G8[(reg, kind, pair)] = []
        for d in A:
            cells_pv, _, _ = pv_cells(d, reg, e1, e2)
            m1, m2 = MAPS[(d["animal"], 8.0, e1)], MAPS[(d["animal"], 8.0, e2)]
            for track in nfn.TRACKS:
                ramp = RN[(RN.animal == d["animal"]) & (RN.region == reg) & (RN.track == track)].unit.values
                other = np.setdiff1d(cells_pv, ramp)
                counts.append({"region": reg, "pair": pair, "animal": d["animal"], "track": track, "ramping": len(ramp), "other": len(other)})
                for kind, cs in (("ramping", ramp), ("other", other)):
                    X, Y = track_norm(m1, track, cs), track_norm(m2, track, cs)
                    pooled.setdefault((reg, kind, pair, track), []).append((X, Y))
                    if len(cs) >= 3:
                        G8[(reg, kind, pair)].append(bin_corr(X, Y))

def report(vals, names):
    keep = [i for i, v in enumerate(vals) if np.isfinite(v).sum() > 0]
    a, dn = nfn.kruskal_dunn([vals[i] for i in keep], [names[i] for i in keep])
    print(f"Kruskal-Wallis H = {a['H']:.1f}, p = {a['p']:.2g}")
    for r in ("CA1", "PFC"):
        pairs = [(f"{r} ramping N-N'", f"{r} ramping F-N'"), (f"{r} ramping N-N'", f"{r} other N-N'"), (f"{r} ramping F-N'", f"{r} other F-N'")]
        for a_, b_ in pairs:
            if a_ in dn.index and b_ in dn.index:
                print(f"   Dunn {a_} vs {b_}: p = {dn.loc[a_, b_]:.3g}")
            else:
                print(f"   Dunn {a_} vs {b_}: not testable (no population of 3 ramping cells)")
report(vals, names)

                if len(X) >= 3:

Result: blocked (too few ramping cells). Ramping samples identified in N' are 4 to 7 per region and trajectory summed over the five rats, and only one animal-trajectory population per region has 3 or more, so the ramping groups are one population of 101 bins each. On it, CA1 ramping F-N' is below N-N' (p = 1.7e-22), PFC ramping does not change (p = 0.34), and ramping and other cells differ only for CA1 F-N' (p = 0.014). With the ramping cells pooled over animals, the CA1 ramping drop is not found (p = 1) and PFC ramping and other cells differ for F-N' (p = 0.016). The two ways of forming the populations disagree, and the ramping selection itself did not reproduce (figs4-ramping-fraction).

def sc_table(s):
    rows = []
    for d in A:
        for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
            cells = np.intersect1d(np.intersect1d(nfn.included(d, reg, 0), nfn.included(d, reg, 1)), nfn.included(d, reg, 2))
            for ep in range(3):
                m = MAPS[(d["animal"], s, ep)]
                for c in cells:
                    si_in, si_out = nfn.selectivity(m, c)
                    si_in_g, si_out_g = nfn.selectivity(m, c, ">")
                    rows.append({"animal": d["animal"], "region": reg, "unit": c, "ep": ep, "si_in": si_in, "si_out": si_out,
                                 "si_in_gt": si_in_g, "si_out_gt": si_out_g, "R": nfn.path_equivalence(m, c)})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
SC = {s: sc_table(s) for s in SMOOTHS}
print("cells in all three sessions:", SC[8.0][SC[8.0].ep == 0].groupby("region").size().to_dict())
print("per animal:", SC[8.0][SC[8.0].ep == 0].groupby(["region", "animal"]).size().unstack(0).to_dict())
def pear(x, y):
    ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    r, p = stats.pearsonr(x[ok], y[ok]); return r, p, int(ok.sum())

The embeddings¶

Single-trial maps of the pseudo-population in N' (and F), as cal_UMAP.m: for each trajectory type the smallest number of passes over the animals, from the first; maps at 1-cm bins (Methods; smoothed at 8 cm as the session maps, as the Methods give no width for them) on 201 bins of normalized length (cal_UMAP.m; about 1 cm on a 2-m trajectory), empty bins inside a pass filled (an assumption, see nfn.single_trial_matrix); states with fewer than 5 active cells dropped. UMAP (umap-learn) with 3 dimensions, cosine metric, 50 neighbours, min_dist 0.6, seed 0; F is embedded with the N' fit (transform). Seeds 1 and 2 are variants.

UMAP's numba code is compiled for the host CPU, and the optimization amplifies rounding differences, so before this round the embeddings, and every number derived from them, differed between machines (the verifier's copy of round 2 differed from the author's). The header cell now compiles for a generic x86-64 target and fixes the BLAS kernel and numpy's dispatch. On one machine the embedding repeats exactly: a second fit with seed 0 below gives the same coordinates (and, a check made outside the notebook, two full executions gave identical outputs in every code cell). Seeds 1 and 2 show how far the results move with the embedding.

In [31]:
import umap
POPSEL = {reg: POP[(reg, "b")] for reg in ("CA1", "PFC")}
ST = {}
for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
    for ep in (2, 1):
        tbt = {d["animal"]: nfn.trials_of_track(d, ep) for d in A}
        tn = {t: min(len(tbt[a][t]) for a in tbt) for t in nfn.TRACKS}
        Xs = []
        for d in A:
            X, lab = nfn.single_trial_matrix(d, ep, POPSEL[reg][d["animal"]], {t: tbt[d["animal"]][t][:tn[t]] for t in nfn.TRACKS})
            Xs.append(X)
        X = np.hstack(Xs); v = (X > 0).sum(1) >= 5
        ST[(reg, ep)] = (X[v], lab[v], tn, int((~v).sum()))
        print(f"{reg} {nfn.EPOCHS[ep]}: passes per trajectory {({nfn.TRACKS[k]: n for k, n in tn.items()})}; states {v.sum()} kept, {(~v).sum()} dropped (fewer than 5 active cells); cells {X.shape[1]}")
EMB = {}
for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
    for seed in (0, 1, 2):
        t0 = time.time()
        um = umap.UMAP(n_components=3, metric="cosine", n_neighbors=50, min_dist=0.6, random_state=seed)

        EMB[(reg, seed)] = (E, EF, um)
        print(f"{reg} seed {seed}: fit and transform in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

# Distance measures of Figure 3H to 3J and S6, used by the claims below and by the variants.
from scipy.spatial.distance import cdist
def seq_dist(E, lab, tn, align, nb=201):
    idx = {(int(t), int(k), int(b)): i for i, (t, k, b) in enumerate(lab)}
    out = {}
    for name, pairs in (("InSeq", [(1, 4), (3, 2)]), ("OutSeq", [(1, 2), (3, 4)])):
        vals = []
        for a_, b_ in pairs:
            for t1 in range(tn[a_]):
                for t2 in range(tn[b_]):
                    ds = [np.linalg.norm(E[idx[(a_, t1, i)]] - E[idx[(b_, t2, j)]])
                          for i in range(nb) for j in [i if align == "location" else nb - 1 - i]
                          if (a_, t1, i) in idx and (b_, t2, j) in idx]
                    if ds:
                        vals.append(np.mean(ds))
        out[name] = np.array(vals)
    return out
def h_test(E, reg, align):
    X, lab, tn, _ = ST[(reg, 2)]
    sd = seq_dist(E, lab, tn, align)
    return np.median(sd["InSeq"]), np.median(sd["OutSeq"]), stats.ranksums(sd["InSeq"], sd["OutSeq"]).pvalue, len(sd["InSeq"]), len(sd["OutSeq"])
CODE_ALIGN = {"CA1": "location", "PFC": "phase"}
def phase_loc(E, lab, mode, nb=201):
    out = {"phase": [], "location": []}
    sel = {(t, b): np.where((lab[:, 0] == t) & (lab[:, 2] == b))[0] for t in nfn.TRACKS for b in range(nb)}
    for i in range(nb):
        for a_, b_ in ((1, 2), (3, 4)):
            p, q = sel[(a_, i)], sel[(b_, i)]
            if len(p) and len(q): out["location"].append(cdist(E[p], E[q]).ravel())
        for a_, b_ in (((1, 4), (3, 2)) if mode == "methods" else ((1, 2), (3, 4))):
            p, q = sel[(a_, i)], sel[(b_, nb - 1 - i)]
            if len(p) and len(q): out["phase"].append(cdist(E[p], E[q]).ravel())
    return {k: np.concatenate(v) for k, v in out.items()}
def fn_dist(E, lab, EF, labF):
    kE, kF = lab[:, 0] * 1000 + lab[:, 2], labF[:, 0] * 1000 + labF[:, 2]
    out = np.full(len(E), np.nan)
    for k in np.unique(kE):
        p, q = np.where(kE == k)[0], np.where(kF == k)[0]
        if len(q): out[p] = cdist(E[p], EF[q]).mean(1)
    return out
def shuffled_activity(X, lab, rng):
    Xs = X.copy()
    for t, k in {(int(a_), int(b_)) for a_, b_, _ in lab}:
        rows = np.where((lab[:, 0] == t) & (lab[:, 1] == k))[0]
        Xs[rows] = X[rows][:, rng.permutation(X.shape[1])]
    return Xs

Manifold variants: gap filling and smoothing of the single-trial maps¶

The manifold results are repeated without the linear filling of empty 1-cm bins inside a pass (an assumption, nfn.single_trial_matrix). The Methods give no smoothing for the single-trial maps; the session maps' 1D width is garbled in the text (fig2d-pv-similarity), so 4 and 2 cm are run too. Each variant rebuilds the states, fits UMAP (seed 0) and repeats the tests of 3H, 3I and 3J, the same distances in the neural space (Figure S6), and the 16 CCGP decoders (100 shuffles each, for time, so the smallest p is 0.01; p_ge counts ties, and a decoder above every shuffle has p_ge = 0).

In [33]:
# Variants of the single-trial maps behind the manifolds: empty 1-cm bins inside a pass left empty
# (set to 0, as cal_UMAP.m does with NaN) instead of filled, and other smoothing widths. Each variant
# rebuilds the states, fits UMAP (seed 0) and repeats the tests of 3H, 3I, 3J and the 16 CCGP
# decoders (100 shuffles each, for time).
def build_states(reg, ep, fill, s):
    tbt = {d["animal"]: nfn.trials_of_track(d, ep) for d in A}
    tn = {t: min(len(tbt[a][t]) for a in tbt) for t in nfn.TRACKS}
    Xs = []
    for d in A:
        X, lab = nfn.single_trial_matrix(d, ep, POPSEL[reg][d["animal"]], {t: tbt[d["animal"]][t][:tn[t]] for t in nfn.TRACKS},
                                         smooth_cm=s, fill_gaps=fill)
        Xs.append(X)
    X = np.hstack(Xs); v = (X > 0).sum(1) >= 5
    return X[v], lab[v], tn, int((~v).sum())

def h_test2(E, lab, tn, align):
    sd = seq_dist(E, lab, tn, align)
    return np.median(sd["InSeq"]), np.median(sd["OutSeq"]), stats.ranksums(sd["InSeq"], sd["OutSeq"]).pvalue

MANVAR = []
for vname, fill, s in (("main: gaps filled, 8 cm", True, 8.0), ("gaps not filled, 8 cm", False, 8.0),
                       ("gaps filled, 4 cm", True, 4.0), ("gaps filled, 2 cm", True, 2.0), ("gaps not filled, 2 cm", False, 2.0)):
    for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
        if fill and s == 8.0:
            X, lab, tn, ndrop = ST[(reg, 2)]; XF, labF, _, _ = ST[(reg, 1)]
            E, EF, um = EMB[(reg, 0)]
        else:
            X, lab, tn, ndrop = build_states(reg, 2, fill, s); XF, labF, _, _ = build_states(reg, 1, fill, s)
            um = umap.UMAP(n_components=3, metric="cosine", n_neighbors=50, min_dist=0.6, random_state=0)
            E = um.fit_transform(X); EF = um.transform(XF)
        i_, o_, ph = h_test2(E, lab, tn, CODE_ALIGN[reg])
        pl = phase_loc(E, lab, "methods")
        Xs = shuffled_activity(X, lab, np.random.default_rng([501, 0]))
        ES = um.transform(Xs)
        real, shuf = fn_dist(E, lab, EF, labF), fn_dist(E, lab, ES, lab)
        rr, ss = real[np.isfinite(real)], shuf[np.isfinite(shuf)]
        hi_, ho_, hp_ = h_test2(X, lab, tn, CODE_ALIGN[reg])       # Figure S6: the same tests in the neural space
        pl_ = phase_loc(X, lab, "methods")
        nr, ns = fn_dist(X, lab, XF, labF), fn_dist(X, lab, Xs, lab); nr, ns = nr[np.isfinite(nr)], ns[np.isfinite(ns)]
        cc = nfn.run_ccgp(nfn.clusters(E, lab), nfn.clusters(EF, labF), n_perm=100, seed=901)
        sig = (cc.p_ge < 0.05)
        MANVAR.append({"variant": vname, "region": reg, "states dropped": ndrop,
                       "3H InSeq": i_, "3H OutSeq": o_, "3H p": ph,
                       "3I phase": np.median(pl["phase"]), "3I location": np.median(pl["location"]),
                       "3I p": stats.ranksums(pl["phase"], pl["location"]).pvalue,
                       "3J F-N' vs shuffle %": 100 * (np.median(rr) / np.median(ss) - 1), "3J p": stats.ranksums(rr, ss).pvalue,
                       "CCGP phase mean": cc[cc.variable == "phase"].ccgp.mean(), "CCGP sequence mean": cc[cc.variable == "sequence"].ccgp.mean(),
                       "CCGP environment mean": cc[cc.variable == "environment"].ccgp.mean(),
                       "decoders p_ge < 0.05": int(sig.sum()), "decoders above every shuffle": int((cc.p_ge == 0).sum()),
                       "S6 3H InSeq - OutSeq": hi_ - ho_, "S6 3H p": hp_,
                       "S6 3I phase - location": np.median(pl_["phase"]) - np.median(pl_["location"]),
                       "S6 3I p": stats.ranksums(pl_["phase"], pl_["location"]).pvalue,
                       "S6 3J F-N' vs shuffle %": 100 * (np.median(nr) / np.median(ns) - 1), "S6 3J p": stats.ranksums(nr, ns).pvalue})
MV = pd.DataFrame(MANVAR)
with pd.option_context("display.float_format", lambda v: f"{v:.3g}"):
    print(MV.iloc[:, :15].to_string(index=False))
    print(MV[["variant", "region"] + list(MV.columns[15:])].to_string(index=False))

fig3h-inseq-outseq-distance¶

In the PFC manifold, trajectories of the same task sequence (InSeq) are closer than trajectories out of sequence (OutSeq); in the CA1 manifold, OutSeq pairs with the same spatial coverage are closer than InSeq pairs.

For every pair of passes of the two types, the mean Euclidean distance over matched bins (cal_UMAP_INSeq_distance.m): CA1 matched by location, PFC by phase (the code); both regions by phase and both by location are variants. Rank-sum test per region.

Result: reproduced, resting on the filling of empty bins in the single-trial maps. In CA1 (aligned by location), OutSeq pairs are closer than InSeq pairs (13.67 against 17.27, rank-sum p = 0.0005); in PFC (aligned by phase), InSeq pairs are closer (14.04 against 17.51, p = 8.9e-06). With the main alignment both regions keep the direction under seeds 1 and 2 (CA1 p = 1.4e-05 and 0.0026, PFC p = 0.00033 and 0.042). Of the other alignments, PFC by location is weaker under seed 2 (p = 0.069); the rest give p < 0.01. The 4-cm and 2-cm widths agree (p <= 3.2e-11), and so do the maps without gap filling at 8 cm (CA1 p = 4.2e-27, PFC 11.0 against 11.1, p = 0.022); without gap filling at 2 cm PFC InSeq and OutSeq do not differ (16.4 and 16.7, p = 0.34), so the outcome rests on the filling. The result also moves with the embedding: in the verifier's round-2 copy, embedded on another machine before the CPU target was fixed, CA1 with the main alignment gave p = 0.096 under seed 1. Seed 0, the standard choice the criterion names, passed in every execution.

PFC neural states at the same trajectory phase are closer than those at the same spatial location, while CA1 shows the opposite.

The PFC manifold is preserved across environments (F states lie closer to N' states than cell-ID shuffles do), while the distortion of the CA1 manifold is similar to that of random shuffles.

Result: partially reproduced, resting on the filling of empty bins. PFC F states lie closer to N' states than the shuffle does (11.86 against 15.28, 22.4% closer, p near 0). CA1 F states are also closer than the shuffle, by less (13.44 against 14.05, 4.4% closer, p = 1.4e-30), so the claim that CA1 does not differ from the shuffle fails by the paper's test. Seeds 1 and 2 give the same (CA1 6.8% and 4.1% closer, PFC 31.5% and 11.7%). CA1 is closer than the shuffle in every width and gap-filling variant (1.9% to 10.8%, p <= 4.6e-19), and PFC is in all but one (7.8% to 60.2% closer): without gap filling at 2 cm PFC F-N' is not closer than the shuffle (0.8% farther, p = 0.029), so there neither part holds and the outcome rests on the filling. That variant moves with the embedding: in the verifier's round-2 copy, embedded on another machine before the CPU target was fixed, it gave PFC 4.9% closer (p = 6.2e-12).

fig3fg-manifold-shapes¶

UMAP embeddings show that PFC population activity lies on a ring-shaped manifold, whereas the CA1 manifold has a double V shape resembling the W-maze.

The embeddings are shown above. The paper gives no measure of the shapes; by the criterion the outcome is that of fig3h-inseq-outseq-distance and fig3i-phase-location-distance.

Result: reproduced (through 3H and 3I). Both distance tests that the criterion takes as the measure of the shapes reproduce. The embeddings and the mean state per trajectory are shown; no measure of a ring or a double V is computed, and the plotted embeddings are made of one thread per pass, not a clean ring or double V. The outcome carries the dependence of fig3h-inseq-outseq-distance on the gap filling (and its seed sensitivity, stated there).

Result: partially reproduced. In the neural space, 3H holds (CA1 OutSeq closer, 45.04 against 52.15, p = 2.5e-12; PFC InSeq closer, 64.27 against 70.61, p = 4.8e-12) and 3I holds (PFC phase 65.47 against location 86.09; CA1 location 45.02 against phase 48.37, p = 9.3e-129). For 3J, PFC F-N' is far below the shuffle (56.6% closer) but CA1 F-N' is below it too (9.2% closer, p = 7.5e-78), so two of the three relationships hold. Every width and gap-filling variant gives the same three directions (CA1 3J 7.3% to 9.2% closer, p <= 2.7e-21).

Abstraction (Figure 4, S7)¶

fig4d-pfc-ccgp and fig4d-ca1-ccgp-chance¶

In PFC, the cross-condition generalization performance (CCGP) for trajectory phase, task sequence and environment is high and above trial-label shuffles for every decoder.

In CA1, CCGP for trajectory phase, task sequence and environment is at or below chance by the trial-label permutation test.

Clusters are the embedded states (seed 0) at 20-30% and 70-80% of the normalized position of each trajectory (cal_all_dichotomies.m), in N' and, for the environment, in F. Decoders and permutation test as nfn.ccgp_sets and nfn.svm_ccgp (1000 shuffles; p is the fraction of shuffles above the real CCGP, p_ge counts ties too). The code's task-sequence test pairs take the two clusters at different segments (CCGP_taskSeq.m); taking them at the same segment is a variant (100 shuffles, for time). The code's environment task-sequence decoders come in identical pairs (rows 1 and 3, 2 and 4 share their training set and F test set), as here.

Result: blocked, methods underspecified (the smoothing width of the single-trial maps). With 8-cm maps, 10 of the 16 PFC decoders have p < 0.001 by the code's strict count, but one of them (the task-sequence decoder tested on the inbound pair at the late segment) predicts one class for every test point, so its CCGP is 0.500, every shuffle ties and p = 1 counting ties. Counting ties, 9 of 16 have p < 0.001. The failing decoders are the phase decoders tested on IN_R, OUT_R and OUT_L (CCGP 0.500 each, p >= 0.54 counting ties), that sequence decoder, and three environment phase decoders (0.560, 0.560 and 0.541; p = 0.004, 0.004 and 0.020), so the claim does not reproduce at 8 cm. Above every one of 100 shuffles (cell 79) are 14 of 16 decoders at 4 cm and 15 of 16 at 2 cm, and 4 of 16 without gap filling at 8 cm and at 2 cm. In this run no width gives all 16. In the verifier's round-2 copy, embedded on another machine before the CPU target was fixed, all 16 were above every one of 200 shuffles at 2 cm, so at the narrow widths the result sits at the edge of the criterion and changes with the embedding. The Methods give no smoothing for the single-trial maps and the session maps' width is garbled; at 8 cm the claim fails clearly, at 2 cm it can pass, so the claim stays methods underspecified, as the claims file's rule for the width (fig2d-pv-similarity) has it.

figs7b-geometric-null¶

Against a geometric random model that keeps within-condition noise but destroys the geometry, PFC CCGP is significant while CA1 CCGP is not.

The noise cloud of each cluster (its states about the centroid) has its axes permuted, separately per cluster, 100 times, and CCGP is recomputed. Readings: (a) the 3 UMAP coordinates; (b) the neuron axes of the cluster's population vectors, embedded with the N' fit. The CCGP of a variable is the mean over its decoders (an assumption; the legend plots the decoders with their median), compared with the 95th percentile of the same mean under the null.

In [42]:
from joblib import Parallel, delayed

def null_b_batch(um, nCN, nCF, seed, n):
    """Reading (b): permute the neuron axes of each cluster's noise cloud, embed with the N' fit."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed); keys = list(nCN); out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        pN, pF = nfn.permute_noise(nCN, rng), nfn.permute_noise(nCF, rng)
        allN = um.transform(np.vstack([pN[k] for k in keys])); allF = um.transform(np.vstack([pF[k] for k in keys]))
        sN = np.cumsum([0] + [len(pN[k]) for k in keys]); sF = np.cumsum([0] + [len(pF[k]) for k in keys])
        eN = {k: allN[sN[i]:sN[i + 1]] for i, k in enumerate(keys)}; eF = {k: allF[sF[i]:sF[i + 1]] for i, k in enumerate(keys)}
        out.append(nfn.ccgp_values(eN, eF).groupby("variable").ccgp.mean())
    return out

def cluster_rows(lab):
    return {(t, s): (lab[:, 0] == t) & np.isin(lab[:, 2], b) for t in nfn.TRACKS for s, b in (("a", nfn.EARLY_BINS), ("b", nfn.LATE_BINS))}
GN = {}
for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
    CN, CF = CL[reg]
    real = nfn.ccgp_values(CN, CF).groupby("variable").ccgp.mean()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(701 if reg == "CA1" else 702)
    draws = [(nfn.permute_noise(CN, rng), nfn.permute_noise(CF, rng)) for _ in range(100)]   # drawn in order, fitted in parallel
    null_a = pd.DataFrame(Parallel(n_jobs=4)(delayed(lambda pN, pF: nfn.ccgp_values(pN, pF).groupby("variable").ccgp.mean())(pN, pF) for pN, pF in draws))
    X, lab, _, _ = ST[(reg, 2)]; XF, labF, _, _ = ST[(reg, 1)]
    um = EMB[(reg, 0)][2]
    rN, rF = cluster_rows(lab), cluster_rows(labF)
    nCN = {k: X[m] for k, m in rN.items()}; nCF = {k: XF[m] for k, m in rF.items()}
    keys = list(nCN)
    t0 = time.time()
    batches = Parallel(n_jobs=4)(delayed(null_b_batch)(um, nCN, nCF, [703, reg == "PFC", i], 25) for i in range(4))
    null_b = [row for b in batches for row in b]
    null_b = pd.DataFrame(null_b)
    GN[reg] = (real, null_a, null_b)
    print(f"{reg} (reading b in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s)")
    print(pd.DataFrame({"CCGP (mean of decoders)": real, "null (a) 95th pct": null_a.quantile(0.95), "p (a)": (null_a >= real).mean(),
                        "null (b) 95th pct": null_b.quantile(0.95), "p (b)": (null_b >= real).mean()}).round(3))

figs7d-dichotomies-decodable¶

With traditional cross-validated decoders, most of the 35 dichotomies of the 8 clusters are decoded accurately in both CA1 and PFC, with similar accuracy in the two regions.

The 35 balanced dichotomies of the 8 N' clusters, each decoded by a linear C-SVM with 4-fold cross-validation on the 3 UMAP coordinates. The trial-label permutation test uses 50 shuffles in place of the paper's 1,000 (a deviation, for time: 100 took about 3 minutes per region here, and the notebook must run in 30 minutes); p is resolved to 0.02, enough to decide p < 0.05 (at most 2 of 50 shuffles above). Rank-sum test of PFC against CA1 accuracies.

In [43]:
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
DI = {}
for reg in ("CA1", "PFC"):
    CN = CL[reg][0]
    t0 = time.time()
    res = Parallel(n_jobs=4)(delayed(nfn.decode_dichotomy)(CN, g, 50, [801, i, reg == "PFC"]) for i, g in enumerate(nfn.dichotomies()))
    DI[reg] = pd.DataFrame({"accuracy": [r[0] for r in res], "p": [r[1] for r in res], "p_ge": [r[3] for r in res], "null_95": [np.percentile(r[2], 95) for r in res]})
    x = DI[reg]
    print(f"{reg} ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s): accuracy median {x.accuracy.median():.3f} (range {x.accuracy.min():.3f} to {x.accuracy.max():.3f}); "
          f"p < 0.05 for {(x.p < 0.05).sum()} of 35 ({(x.p_ge < 0.05).sum()} counting ties); null 95th percentile median {x.null_95.median():.3f}")
print(f"rank-sum PFC against CA1 accuracies: p = {stats.ranksums(DI['PFC'].accuracy, DI['CA1'].accuracy).pvalue:.3g}; "
      f"median difference {DI['PFC'].accuracy.median() - DI['CA1'].accuracy.median():+.3f}")

Result: blocked, methods underspecified (depends on fig4d-pfc-ccgp). The claim depends on fig4d-pfc-ccgp, which is blocked. At 8 cm most dichotomies are decoded above the shuffles in both regions (CA1 35 of 35, PFC 34 of 35, the same counting ties), but the accuracies differ: CA1 is higher (median 0.830 against 0.631, rank-sum p = 8.6e-09), so the similarity part would fail; the other widths were not run for this test.

How the analysis differs from the paper's¶

  • Linearization. The dandiset has no linearized positions; positions are projected onto W-shaped paths built from the well positions and the run positions (an assumption; 180 to 220 cm per trajectory, median 5 cm from the path).
  • The 1D smoothing width is garbled in the paper's text, and no smoothing is given for the single-trial maps; 8, 4 and 2 cm are run. Where the outcome changes with the width (figs4d, figs5e, fig3d, fig3e, fig4d-pfc-ccgp), the claim is blocked as methods underspecified, by the claims file's rule for fig2d-pv-similarity, and the claims that depend on fig4d-pfc-ccgp are blocked with it.
  • Sharp-wave ripple times are not excluded from the rate maps (no ripple times in the dandiset), and the decoder's theta restriction (a variant in the code) cannot be applied (no theta times).
  • The code's per-animal interneuron lists cannot be applied (no cell numbers); the code's 7 Hz rule for CA1 is.
  • Single-trial maps for the manifolds have the empty 1-cm bins inside a pass filled linearly (an assumption, as cal_PVsimilarity.m fills session maps). Without the filling, 3H, 3I and 3J keep their outcomes at 8 cm, but at 2 cm the PFC parts of 3H and 3J fail (in this run), and the CCGP changes.
  • A CCGP decoder that predicts one class for every test point has CCGP 0.5 and ties with every shuffle; the code's strict count of shuffles above gives it p = 0. Here such decoders are counted as not significant (ties counted).
  • The UMAP implementation is umap-learn with fixed seeds, not the MATLAB toolbox with the paper's saved templates; the manifold results vary with the seed (seeds 0 to 2 shown). The embeddings also differed between machines until numba's CPU target was fixed (header cell); the verifier's round-2 copy and this run differ in the decimals and, at the edges, in single tests (stated per claim).
  • Figure 1 and S1 behaviour is tested only on N, F and N' of the five rats; the de novo sessions and the F-N-F'-N' rats are not in the dandiset.
  • The dichotomy decoders use 50 label shuffles in place of 1,000, and the manifold variants' CCGP 100, for the 30-minute limit.

What was found about the dataset¶

  • The units table's electrodes column holds tetrode numbers, not row indices of the electrodes table; read as row indices, units are put in the wrong region (up to 32 units per animal).
  • Units have no cell number within a tetrode, no waveform and no interneuron label, so the paper's interneuron exclusion cannot be applied; units clustered only in later epochs are appended to the table with no spike in N, without a note.
  • acquisition/ElectricalSeries is a byte-identical second copy of the 1.5 kHz LFP; there is no 30 kHz recording.
  • The position's reference frame is given as "center well", but positions are camera coordinates in which the center well sits at different places in each room. The five files' session start times fall within 16 minutes of each other on 2023-03-14, two days before the first published version: the time of conversion, not of the recordings. Epochs carry no names; N, F, N' are known only from the description's order. Linearized positions, the idealized track paths, ripple and theta times are not included.
  • The de novo learning sessions and the F-N-F'-N' rats behind Figure 1C, 1B and S1 are not in the dandiset.
